To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a TCS, RgfA/C, activates the major fibrinogen-binding protein, FbsB, in the most virulent clone of GBS.
a specific combination (fbsA, fBSB and rgf) of genes accounts for the high fibrionogen-binding ability of GBS strain of CC17, a group of strains highly invasive for neonates.

(i) the highly invasive GBS CC17 strains have a specific gene combination (fbsAB and rgfAC) that is responsible for their high fibrinogen- binding ability; and (ii) the RgfA/C TCS inhibits fbsA gene transcription and activates fbsB gene transcription, resulting in a 52% - 68% decrease of fibrinogen binding ability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a new fbs regulator gene (rgf) and the determination of the role of the fbs genes (fbsB and fbsA) in the fibrin-binding ability of CC 17 strains.
the mechanisms by which GBS strains are able to bind to fibrins, which is one of the key steps of the pathogenicity of this bacterium.
the identification of a novel TCS (RgfA/C) that controls fbs genes in CC17 strains, and the determination of the relative contribution of the fbsA and ffsB genes in fibrin binding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RgfA/C TCS is an activator of fbsB and an inhibitor of fbsA genes in CC17 strains.
CC17 strains have a specific combination of genes that are involved in fibrinogen binding and that this specific combination is responsible for their enhanced fibrinogen-binding activity.
the RgfAC system inhibits the FbsA protein production, but stimulates FbsB protein expression, resulting in the high fibrinogenicity observed in the CC17 strains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RgfAC two component system is a global regulator of the fbsA and fsbB genes in GBS.
a two-component system RgfA/C activates the fbs gene expression in highly virulent CC17 group B streptococci.
the CC17 strains of GBS are characterized by a specific combination of genes encoding fbsA, rgfAC and fbsB proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we identified a new regulator of fibrinogen binding in GBS, and that this regulator is a TCS, which is the first one to be described in this species.
the highly virulent CC17 strains of GBS are distinguished by a specific combination of fibrinogen binding and regulator genes.
the RgfAC TCS regulates the expression of fbsA and f bsB genes, and that the FbsB protein is the main fibrinogen-binding protein of GBS CC17 strains.
